findings.title: Google credential key is overwritten with the safeParse wrapper object
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed data. Before this change the code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which returned the data itself. Now `key` is the wrapper, and `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` persists `{ success, data }` as the credential key. On the next instantiation, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in `googleAuth` throws. Every Google Calendar credential therefore breaks on its first token refresh, including on instances that never enable credential sync. Store `key.data`, or make the helper return the data.

findings.title: Computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` produce a single bogus "[object Object]" field
findings.body: `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the string "[object Object]". Both computed keys collapse into one property named "[object Object]", and the second definition (`z.unknown().optional()`) overwrites the first. The effective schema is `{ access_token: string }`, and zod's default strip mode then drops every other field, including expiry_date, expires_in, instance_url and scope. In sync mode the output is always just `{access_token, refresh_token: "refresh_token"}`. Consequences: Zoom computes `expiry_date = Date.now() + undefined*1000 = NaN`, which is stored as null and fails `zoomTokenSchema` next time. Office365 never updates expiry and refreshes on every call. Salesforce loses `instance_url`. Use `.passthrough()` or `.catchall()` and validate the expiry field explicitly.

findings.title: Placeholder "refresh_token" overwrites real refresh tokens when the provider omits one
findings.body: When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the helper injects the literal string "refresh_token". This also runs outside sync mode. Office365's `refreshTokenResponseSchema` marks `refresh_token` optional, and the caller spreads the result over the stored credentials (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`). If Microsoft does not return a new refresh token, the user's real refresh token is replaced with "refresh_token" and every later refresh fails. Previously the missing key was simply absent and the old token survived. In sync mode the same placeholder is written into Zoom's stored `refresh_token`.

findings.title: Choice of schema doesn't match where the tokens actually came from
findings.body:
`refreshOAuthTokens` only calls the sync endpoint when `userId` is non-null. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` switches to the minimal schema whenever sync is enabled, regardless of where the tokens came from. Two cases get a genuine provider response parsed (and stripped) with the minimal schema:
- Team credentials (userId null), whose refresh went to the real provider.
- Salesforce, which calls the provider directly and never goes through `refreshOAuthTokens`.

Those stored credentials lose required fields. The two helpers need a shared decision, for example by passing a flag or returning the source along with the response.

findings.title: Sync path returns a raw fetch Response, which callers don't expect
findings.body:
Callers' refresh functions return different shapes:
- Google returns a GaxiosResponse and reads `res.data`.
- HubSpot returns a `TokenResponseIF` and reads `.expiresIn` / `.accessToken`.
- Zoho CRM and Bigin return axios responses and read `.data.error`.
- Lark expects the `{code:0, data:{...}}` envelope.

In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` always returns a fetch `Response`, so these paths break:
- Google throws a TypeError on `token.access_token`, which is swallowed, and continues with an expired token.
- HubSpot writes a serialized Response object (with NaN expiry) as the credential key.
- Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM throw on `tokenInfo.data.error`.
- Lark's `handleLarkError` rejects the response.

The sync response must be normalized to each adapter's expected shape, or each adapter must handle it explicitly.

findings.title: Outbound token-sync request carries no authentication
findings.body: The request to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no shared secret, signature or auth header. The self-hoster's endpoint returns live third-party access tokens. To work with Cal.com it has to accept unauthenticated requests keyed by a sequential integer user ID, so anyone who can reach it can enumerate IDs and harvest every user's OAuth tokens. The inbound webhook uses a secret and encryption, but the outbound direction has neither. Send the webhook secret (or an HMAC) and expect the response to be encrypted with `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

findings.title: `prisma` used without being imported
findings.body: The new `prisma.credential.update(...)` call references `prisma`, but this file never imports `@calcom/prisma`. It can only resolve through the dev-only `globalThis.prisma` cache, which is typed `PrismaClient | undefined` and is not set in production. In production `getClient` throws a ReferenceError, so the Salesforce integration fails for every operation.

findings.title: Salesforce refreshes on every instantiation, then ignores the new token
findings.body: `getClient` now unconditionally POSTs a refresh_token grant every time the service is constructed, which happens on every booking create/update/delete. It does not check expiry, adding latency and risking Salesforce rate limits. After refreshing and saving the new token, the `jsforce.Connection` is still built from `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url`, the stale values loaded before the refresh. Pass `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` and `instance_url` instead, and refresh only when needed.

findings.title: Success check relies on `statusText === "OK"`
findings.body: `statusText` is an empty string for HTTP/2 responses and can differ between proxies and runtimes. In those cases a successful 200 response is treated as an error and throws `HttpError` with an empty message. Use `response.ok` instead.

findings.title: Credential ID is passed where the user ID is expected
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credential.id` as the third argument, which is the Cal.com user ID. The sync endpoint therefore receives `calcomUserId=<credential id>` and may return tokens for the wrong user. Because a credential ID is never null, the `userId` guard meant to skip team credentials is also bypassed. Pass `credential.userId`; this requires threading it into `refreshAccessToken`.

findings.title: Zoom sync uses slug "zoomvideo" instead of the app slug "zoom"
findings.body: The Zoom app's slug/appId is "zoom", which is what `createOAuthAppCredential` uses and what the webhook matches against `prisma.app.slug`. The refresh call sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, the directory name. A self-hoster implementing the sync endpoint therefore sees a slug that doesn't match the one they must send to `/api/webhook/app-credential`.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`
findings.body: The secret header is checked with a plain string inequality. That leaks timing information an attacker can use to guess the secret, and this endpoint can write arbitrary credentials for any user. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. The handler also accepts any HTTP method; restrict it to POST.

findings.title: Invalid body or undecryptable keys surface as 500s
findings.body: `schema.parse(req.body)` and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` both throw on bad input, such as a malformed payload, a wrong encryption key or non-JSON plaintext. There is no try/catch, so the caller gets an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 with a useful message. That makes integration failures hard to diagnose for self-hosters. Use `safeParse` and catch decryption errors.

findings.title: Synced credential update doesn't clear the `invalid` flag
findings.body: Adapters such as Google, Zoom and Webex mark credentials `invalid: true` on `invalid_grant`. When the parent app pushes fresh keys through this webhook, only `key` is updated, so the credential stays flagged invalid even though it now holds valid tokens. Set `invalid: false` on update.

findings.title: No tests for the new sync helpers or the webhook
findings.body: The PR changes token refresh for about ten integrations and adds a credential-writing webhook, but includes no unit tests. The PR description says as much. Simple tests would have caught several of the bugs above: the `[object Object]` schema key, the safeParse wrapper being persisted as Google's key, and the Response shape mismatch in sync mode.
